# Expedia.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/expedia-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/expedia-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects hotel and flight data from expedia.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Code:** [`expedia.py`](expedia.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Flights](results/flights.json) · [Hotels](results/hotels.json)

## What it scrapes

- Expedia.com hotel search results
- Hotel name, URL, prices, star rating, review score/count, and location
- Expedia.com flight search results (one-way and round-trip)

## Functions

- `scrape_hotel_search(destination, check_in, check_out, adults=2, max_pages=3)` → `List[Hotel]`
- `scrape_flight_search(origin, destination, departure_date, return_date=None, adults=1, cabin_class='economy', max_pages=3)` → `List[Flight]`

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`Hotel`**: `hotel_id?`, `name?`, `url?`, `nightly_price?`, `total_price?`, `star_rating?`, `review_score?`, `review_count?`, `location?`, `market_country?`, `captured_at`
- **`Flight`**: `origin`, `destination`, `airline?`, `price?`, `departure_time?`, `arrival_time?`, `duration?`, `stops?`, `cabin_class`, `captured_at`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`expedia.py`](expedia.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)

## Notes

Expedia.com can be difficult to scrape because of scraper blocking so this scraper is using Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker) feature and browser rendering to capture Expedia's internal GraphQL API responses.

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/expedia-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_scrape_hotel_search`, `test_scrape_flight_search`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
